title: What is in your founder shopping cart?
intro: Where the money goes when nobody is watching. Everyone has a category and nobody picks it on purpose.
og_line: Five questions and where your money quietly goes.

cta.title: Something a bit more serious
cta.label: The Energy Discovery
cta.blurb: That one was for fun. The Energy Discovery is 48 statements and returns how you actually work across all twelve energies.

questions.q: Last thing you bought for the business:

options.a: Sign up to learn it properly
Two trials I forgot to cancel
A notebook too nice to use
How much I spend on reading
What I paid to learn things
I finished the ones that mattered
One of them is going to be worth it

results.name: Books
results.headline: Bought, stacked, mostly unread.
results.body: You buy the answer in advance and get to it later. The pile is a to do list you paid for.
results.cost: Reading about it has started to feel like doing it.

results.name: AI tools
results.headline: A subscription for every problem.
results.body: There is a tool for this and you have it. Possibly two, because the second one had a better demo.
results.cost: Nobody has ever cancelled the first one.

results.name: Office supplies
results.headline: The setup has to be right first.
results.body: The desk, the chair, the notebook that is finally the correct notebook. Getting ready is a real feeling and you like it.
results.cost: Getting ready is not the same as starting, and it is more fun.

results.name: Courses
results.headline: Module three, every time.
results.body: You buy the structured version because structure is the bit you find hardest to make yourself.
results.cost: The completion rate is the number worth looking at.

results.name: Domain names
results.headline: Eleven of them. Two are good.
results.body: Each one was a real idea at the moment you bought it. The renewals arrive together every year like a report card.
results.cost: Owning the address is the cheapest possible version of starting.
